title: needs-decision: audit-pr-cleanup has no ack-only-post-disposition carve-out F2/F3's gate already has
body:
# needs-decision: audit-pr-cleanup has no ack-only-post-disposition carve-out F2/F3's gate already has

## Background

Refs #2586. `hasFreshDisposition` (`src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts`)
computes `latestFeedbackAt` as the max activity timestamp of every
non-disposition comment in a thread, then requires the disposition
comment's own timestamp to be strictly after that max. In practice, any
single trailing reply that is not itself a recognized `**Accepted**`/
`**Rejected**` disposition — including a content-free advisory-bot
courtesy acknowledgment — invalidates the disposition's freshness.

Reproduced mechanically against a real PR review thread (GraphQL
thread id `PRRT_kwDOCuI_ec6fNMgw`, `isResolved: true`, fetched via `gh
api graphql`, not only from a session self-report): a bot posted the
original finding; a maintainer replied with a properly stamped
`**Rejected** — {reason}` disposition; the same bot then replied a
content-free courtesy withdrawal ("thanks for the clarification ...
I withdraw this finding") with a timestamp after the disposition's own.
`hasFreshDisposition` evaluates `false` for this exact thread.

`audit-pr-cleanup.mts`'s two consumers of this function — the
per-thread minimizer check in `evaluateReviewComment` (reporting
`'review thread is missing an IDD accept/reject disposition'`) and the
per-review-parent aggregate via `indexThreadsByReview`'s
`missingDisposition` counter — have no carve-out for this pattern; a
repository-wide search for `ackOnly`/
`classifyThreadAckOnlyPostDisposition`/`soleCause` against
`audit-pr-cleanup.mts` returns zero matches.

`pre-merge-readiness.mts` hits the identical `hasFreshDisposition`
staleness first, but when it comes back `false`, additionally runs
`classifyThreadAckOnlyPostDisposition`, which checks whether every
post-disposition, post-snapshot-boundary external comment on the
thread is a pure advisory-bot courtesy acknowledgment. When true,
`soleCauseAckOnlyPostDisposition` is set, and
`buildPreMergeReadinessSummary`'s blocker logic — explicitly commented
`(#2125)` — skips the `disposition-evidence` blocker for exactly this
case. This is the mechanism that lets F2/F3 correctly treat the
example thread above as dispositioned, while F4's `audit-pr-cleanup`
(no such override) reports it missing.

`#2125` (closed) fixed the identical symptom shape but was explicitly
scoped to the F2/F3 merge-execute path — its PR's changed-files list
never touched `audit-pr-cleanup.mts`. `#951` (closed) previously
established that `audit-pr-cleanup`'s `hasFreshDisposition` callers are
deliberately treated as "non-gate," a distinct category from the F2/F3
gate's stricter, purpose-built handling — relevant precedent that this
line has been drawn deliberately before, which is why this is a
maintainer decision rather than an assumed oversight. No open or closed
issue was found covering extending the F2/F3 ack-only carve-out to F4.

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision among the
options below, given `#951`'s precedent that F4's stricter treatment
was a deliberate prior choice.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Extend the carve-out.** Give `audit-pr-cleanup.mts`'s two call
   sites the same `classifyThreadAckOnlyPostDisposition`-style
   ack-only check F2/F3 already has, so a resolved thread whose only
   post-disposition activity is a pure advisory-bot courtesy
   acknowledgment is still treated as dispositioned (or reported as a
   separate, distinctly labeled skip reason) for F4 minimization
   purposes.
2. **Keep F4 stricter, fix the message.** Leave the current
   classification behavior unchanged, but stop reporting the
   `'...is missing an IDD accept/reject disposition'` text when a
   disposition **was** found but is merely stale — that message is
   misleading for a human auditing the F4 report, who would reasonably
   conclude no disposition was ever posted.
3. **Minimal: enrich the skip reason only.** Without changing pass/fail
   classification, have the skip carry whether a stale disposition was
   found and what invalidated its freshness (the trailing comment's
   author/timestamp), so the false-positive is legible without
   re-deriving it from GraphQL data by hand.
4. **Something else the maintainer prefers.**

## Acceptance criteria

- A maintainer states which option above to take (or a different
  resolution) in a comment on this issue.
- Close this issue once that decision is recorded. The chosen option
  becomes a follow-up `ready` issue scoped to the exact
  `audit-pr-cleanup.mts` change — this issue itself stays
  decision-only.

## Candidate files

- `src/scripts/audit-pr-cleanup.mts`
- `src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts`

---

_Autopilot suitability: 4 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented. This is a deliberate
gate-vs-non-gate strictness trade-off with a settled precedent (#951);
the field evidence above is already gathered and mechanically verified
against a live thread, and does not need re-deriving._
